Author: Sanjay Kumar Singh
Bench: Sanjay Kumar Singh
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 76
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 31554 of 2022
Applicant :- Rakesh

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Ashish Dwivedi,Dileep Kumar Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Rajesh Kumar Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate representing the State and learned counsel appearing on behalf of the informant.

By means of this second bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., applicant, who is involved in Case Crime No. 0319 of 2019, under sections 304B, 498A IPC and Sections 3/4 D.P. Act, police station Sahawar, district Kasganj, seeks enlargement on bail during the pendency of trial.
The first bail application of the applicant was rejected vide order dated 30.11.2021 considering the merits of the case.

The first and foremost submission of learned counsel for the applicant is that the applicant is in jail since 25.11.2019 therefore considering his detention period, he is entitled to be released on bail.

1

Per contra, learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel appearing on behalf of the informant vehemently opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant by contending that the applicant is the husband of the deceased.
In post mortem report, five injuries were found on the body of the deceased.
It is a case of brutal murder as the cause of death has been shown as asphyxia due to strangulation.

It is also pointed out that in this case, PW-1, PW-2 and PW-3 have already been examined before the trial court and they have supported the prosecution case, therefore, applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.
Having heard learned counsel for the parties and examined the matter in its entirety, I find substance in the submission of learned A.G.A. that it is a case of brutal murder by strangulation.
Since the trial of the applicant is proceeding and three prosecution witnesses have been examined, I do not find any new ground to consider the second bail application of the applicant at this stage.

Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case as well as keeping in view the submissions advanced on behalf of parties, gravity of offence, role assigned to applicant and severity of punishment, I do not find any good ground to release the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is rejected at this stage.
It is made clear that the observation contained in the instant order is confined to the issue of bail and shall not affect the merit of the trial.

However the trial court is directed to make an endeavour to conclude the trial, expeditiously,
without granting any unnecessary adjournment to either of the parties.
Order Date :- 17.1.2023 Saurabh  Rakesh vs State Of U.P. on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173125423/
